Read straight from Health Connect on this phone, so a second wearable that publishes there can be seen rather than assumed. Nothing here is sent anywhere; it is a look at what is already on the phone.

A watch already paired in Android’s Bluetooth settings is listed below without scanning. Otherwise press Scan. reCMF negotiates its own key — you do not need to find one by hand.

As the watch reports them. Goal changes have to be made on the watch: it accepts them from here and then keeps what it had.
Zero turns an alert off. Quiet hours are not configurable yet.
Sent to the watch for its weather screen. reCMF asks a forecast service for one place — it never asks the phone where you are.
Only what you change here is sent to the watch. Anything you leave alone stays as the watch has it.

The watch dates its newest record %1$s (%2$s) — a different day from the phone\'s. Everything above is counted against the phone\'s date, so it will read zero until the two agree. Check the date on the watch.
Not sent to the watch yet — this happens on the next refresh, or as soon as the watch connects.
No place chosen yet, so there is nothing to ask for.
The weather service could not be reached. reCMF will try again on the next refresh; the watch keeps the last forecast it was given.

Android is allowed to defer reCMF\'s scheduled work while the phone is idle, which is why the forecast and the step count can go hours without refreshing. Allowing unrestricted background use fixes that; reCMF still only wakes on its refresh interval.
The watch has not sent any measurements yet today.
Makes the watch ring and vibrate, as long as it is in Bluetooth range.

The watch has its own GPS, but starting from nothing it has to read the satellites\' orbits off the satellites — minutes in the open, and rarely at all between buildings. Give it those orbits and a fix takes seconds. reCMF fetches those orbits itself, from the people who publish them, and sends them on every couple of days. Whatever is sent is checked first.
The watch has not been given orbits yet.
Rings when you ask the watch to find your phone.
Your watch is looking for this phone
Tap to stop. It stops on its own after half a minute.
Shown as the watch reported them when it connected. The watch keeps exactly the list it is sent, so nothing goes to it until you change something here.
Android will ask you to confirm the install. If it refuses, allow reCMF to install apps in system settings.
Tells you once when a newer build of reCMF is published.
Ask about anything the watch has been recording. Every question carries the same table of days the metric cards send, and what you have written about yourself.
The coach is switched off. Turn it on under the assistant, on the watch tab.
The watch hands a night over about twenty minutes after you get up, and only once. Nothing has arrived yet.
The watch names none of its faces, so these are counted in the order it reports them, and it tells reCMF whenever the face changes on the wrist.
The watch holds six and no more, so installing one replaces another. Pick which one goes, then choose the file — a .bin built for the Watch Pro 2.
One day is not a week yet. Wear the watch a few more days and this fills in.

Off until you turn it on. reCMF has never sent anything about you anywhere, and this is the first thing that would — so it is two switches rather than one, and you can see exactly what leaves before it does.
Sends figures and nothing that names you: resting pulse, sleep length, the stress index, steps. A column of numbers.
Also sends your profile — name, height, weight, anything you note about yourself. This is the part that is about a person rather than a wrist.

Sent only while Coach is on. Age, height and weight change how a figure should be read at all — a resting pulse means something different at twenty and at sixty. Everything else is yours to write, or to leave blank.
Recovering from flu. Train Tue and Thu. No advice about diet.
OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq and most local servers use chat completions. Perplexity\'s Agent API uses Responses — and their Sonar endpoints, which use the other one, retire on 27 September 2026.

Only applies to the Responses format, where search is a tool that has to be asked for. It costs more per question, and it means the question reaches a search engine as well as the model. Perplexity shows its sources for its own Sonar models; other models search without being able to cite.
This provider does not publish a list. Type the model name from its documentation.
Stored. It is sealed in the Android keystore and never goes into a backup.
No key yet. Nothing can be asked without one.
Anything speaking the OpenAI chat format works — Perplexity, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or a model running on your own machine. Change the address and the model and it goes there instead.
What the assistant is told before your figures. Editable, because a prompt you cannot read is one you cannot trust.
This is the message itself, not a description of it.
It answered, and the answer had nothing in it.
Fill in the address, the model and a key first.
Writes your settings, alarms, goals and the health history reCMF holds to a file you choose. Restoring merges it into what is here, so importing the same file twice changes nothing the second time.
The watch pairing key is never written to the file. It is held in the Android keystore, which does not leave the phone — so on a new phone you pair again, and everything else is already set up.
That file is not a reCMF backup, or was written by a newer version.

Scored against your own recent days, not against anybody else — 50 means exactly your usual. Only measurements with enough history behind them count; the rest share out their weight rather than voting average, so the rows above are the whole of what this number was built from.

Not the same number Whoop or Fitbit show. Those lean hardest on heart-rate variability, which this watch cannot measure — its pulse arrives as one figure a minute with no intervals behind it. Another wearable on this phone can supply it; without one, this is built from what the watch does measure.

Some of the figures above came from another wearable on this phone, through Health Connect: %1$s. That is also why this number and that device\'s own score can disagree — they are not built from the same things.
Not enough days yet. Wear the watch for a few nights and this fills in.
No night to score yet. It appears the morning after the watch reports one.
How long you slept is scored against your target; the rest against your own recent nights. A part nothing could measure is left out rather than counted as average.
How much of the night was spent awake comes from another wearable on this phone. The CMF watch has no waking stage — it reports deep, light and REM and nothing else.
This night was recorded by another wearable on this phone — the watch reported none. The picture above is the watch\'s own last night, which is a different night.

The last reading the watch took, from the optical sensor against your wrist. A resting adult is usually somewhere between 60 and 100 bpm, and whatever you were doing pushes it up. A wrist is an awkward place to measure this: a loose strap and any movement both spoil a reading, so a single odd number is far more often a bad measurement than a bad heart. The week below is the part worth reading.

The lowest level the watch sees you hold for a while, which in practice is mostly while you sleep. Most adults sit somewhere between 55 and 85, and the fitter you are the lower it tends to run. The figure itself matters less than a change in it: several beats above your own usual level, held for days rather than hours, is what tends to come with illness, a bad night or alcohol. A single day is noise.

The share of the haemoglobin in your blood that is carrying oxygen. At sea level 95 to 100 percent is the ordinary range. A wrist is a poor place to measure it — considerably worse than a fingertip oximeter — and cold hands, movement and a loose strap all push a reading down, so one low figure is usually the measurement rather than you. Several low ones across a quiet night are worth more attention.

The watch\'s own number, from 0 to 100, and the one figure here with nothing to compare it against. CMF publishes neither how it is worked out nor what counts as high, so reCMF reads the value out of the watch and shows it exactly as it arrives, without inventing bands for it. Health Connect has no record type for stress at all, which is a fair measure of how non-standard it is. It is worth something only against yourself: notice what a quiet evening reads and what a bad day reads. On its own, one number means nothing.

Worked out by the watch rather than measured. No satellite is involved in this figure — it follows from your step count and whatever stride length the watch assumes for you. That makes it good for comparing one day against another and poor as a surveyed distance: if the watch\'s idea of your stride is off, every day here is off by the same proportion.

The watch\'s estimate of what you burned, from your movement and the profile it holds. Every wearable estimates this its own way and they disagree with each other by a wide margin — the same walk can differ by a third between two devices. It is a number to watch move over a week, not a budget to spend against.

Floors climbed — and the one figure in reCMF whose meaning is inferred rather than confirmed. Nothing in the watch labels it. What reCMF found is a number that climbs through the day and resets at midnight, sitting in the same place and the same size as the floors count in the watch\'s goal block. That is the whole of the evidence. It behaves like floors and is shown as floors; if it turns out to be something else, this is where the mistake is.
Connect the watch to see the faces it holds and switch between them.

The watch will hold whatever the phone\'s clock holds, and the alarms set on the watch itself are replaced. Android gives no app a way to list another app\'s alarms, so on most phones this needs root. Turn it on and reCMF will say here whether it worked.
Not working: the phone\'s clock will not let reCMF read its alarms, and there is no root on this phone to insist with. Everything else in reCMF works without root — this one setting cannot.
Not working: this phone\'s clock app keeps its alarms somewhere reCMF cannot read. Root would not help. The alarms set on the watch itself still work.

No workouts yet. The watch keeps no summary of a session and will not hand one over, so a workout shows up here once it has sent the pulse it measured during it — which arrives on the next sync after the session ends.
The phone does not know where it is
The place is taken when you open reCMF. To have it follow you with the app closed, allow location access all the time in system settings.
The place follows you, app open or not.

reCMF will stop talking to it and forget the pairing. Getting it back means pairing again, granting the permissions again, and sending the watch a fresh almanac. Nothing already written to Health Connect is lost.
